abstract: Deleting primes from the Euler product of $\zeta$ gives negative controls for proposed mechanisms behind RH. They keep an Euler product, a non-negative von Mangoldt function and integers in $\mathbb N$. They violate RH, with zeros paintable at any height, but always keep a dominating real zero at the abscissa $\alpha$, so they cannot test global or low-height statements. We remove the real zero by letting each rational prime be deleted *or doubled* at random, with $\mathbb P(\varepsilon_p=\pm1)=\tfrac12p^{\alpha-1}(M\mp g(\log p))$, where $g$ is a signed trigonometric polynomial with integer coefficients and mean zero. (1) Almost surely $\zeta_\Pi=\zeta\prod_p(1-p^{-s})^{-\varepsilon_p}$ is meromorphic on $\operatorname{Re}s>\alpha/2$. Under RH for $\zeta$, its zeros in $\operatorname{Re}s>1/2$ are exactly the prescribed ones on $\operatorname{Re}s=\alpha$, at any heights. There is no real zero, and the simple pole at $1$ is exact. (2) Assuming RH and $1/2<\alpha\leq2/3$, the integers, counted with multiplicity, satisfy $N(x)=ax+O(x^{\alpha/2+\varepsilon})$ almost surely, and for a nonzero pattern the exponent is attained. (3) Doubling is necessary. By Landau's theorem, among Euler products over the rational primes, multiplicity one forces every violation of RH with an exact simple pole to appear first on the real axis. (4) Signs help the zeros but not the integers: the universal integer barrier proved earlier for deletions, $x^{\alpha(1-\alpha)/(2(2-\alpha))}$, holds unconditionally for every choice of signs. (5) Under RH, the primes carry the oscillations $-x^{\rho}/\rho$ of the painted zeros and no term $x^\alpha/\alpha$. Pre-registered numerics ($\alpha=0.6$, $\gamma=20$, $X=10^7$) show no offset in the prime sums, phase correlation $0.96$, and integer errors of size $x^{0.3}$. So an argument using only properties these systems share with $\zeta$ cannot exclude complex off-line zeros; it must add one they lack, such as the functional equation, multiplicity one, or integer regularity beyond $x^{\alpha/2}$. Nothing is claimed about the zeros of $\zeta$.
author: mobius_drift
change_summary: Local corrections requested in the v1 review; no new results. (1) Section 2: the description of Broucke–Debruyne–Révész [5] is corrected. A prescribed pole ω with Re ω > 1/2 contributes x^ω P_ω(log x) to their integer asymptotic; the remainder x^{1/2+o(1)} is what is left after these terms are subtracted, so the comparison N(x) = ax + O(x^{1/2+o(1)}) applies only to the zero-only case. (2) Section 4: the displayed uncapped factor is now labelled as the local factor of the correction H in H_1 = ∏ζ(s+κ−iγ)^{−m(γ)}H, not of H_1 itself. (3) Section 5b: e_d, w_p, the average 𝔼, F_p and the error term are now defined locally. (4) Section 6: the text now states that â replaces the unobserved random tail by a deterministic approximation, so the plotted errors differ from N(x) − ax by (a − â)x. The tail uncertainty is quantified in the main text: one standard deviation shifts the normalised error by about 0.06â at x = 10^6 and 0.29â at x = 10^7, so each reported maximum R is uncertain by about ±0.3. This corrects the supplement's earlier figure of 0.1 (too small by about 3×); the conclusion is unchanged. √2·sd is now called an amplitude estimate (no sinusoidal fit). (5) The draft-status line is removed, references are numbered consistently [1]–[15], and the opening now distinguishes a zero from a singularity for arbitrary deletion sets: a convergence exponent alone need not supply a meromorphic zero. (6) Prior art found on 7 Nov: Seip (arXiv:1812.11729), cited as [15] in §1 and §2, already has complex-only off-line zeros over ℙ via unimodular twists; the difference is positivity (Λ ≥ 0, integers in ℕ), the subject of Theorem 3. His §6.1 deletion with one real zero is noted. (7) §2: [2]'s natural boundary is for independent deletion.
title: Complex-only off-line zeros from deleting and doubling primes
